comments.author: mpweiher
comments.why_zh: Uncle Bob 那场出色的架构演讲
comments.quote_zh: 另见 Uncle Bob 那场出色的架构演讲
comments.text_zh: 漂亮的反驳！我本来要写的会稍微不那么客气 :-) 怎么强调都不为过：TDD 不是关于测试（这一点 DHH 搞错了，很多——如果不是大多数——批评者也都搞错了）。它是关于开发和设计的。你能从中得到一个相当不错的测试套件，这只是个不错的副作用。（我就爱这些副作用，没有它们我都不想写程序。）我还发现，每当我偷懒省事，它总会反过来咬我。而且通常是因为我没有足够理解问题空间，写不出合适的测试。这对我来说是 TDD 的一个重要部分：我必须足够理解需求，才能真正为它们写测试。另外，原帖作者说得也对：就我所能判断的，Rails 对 TDD 来说是个糟糕的环境，因为所有那些魔法和自动集成都会碍事，还得费劲地 stub/mock 等等。也许社区是时候放下 Rails 了。（另见 Uncle Bob 那场出色的架构演讲：[VIDEO] ）。
comments.text: Excellent riposte! Mine was going to be somewhat less polite :-) Can't stress enough that TDD is not about testing (sth. DHH, like many if not most critics gets wrong). It is about development and design. The fact that you get a pretty decent test suite out of it is a nice side effect. (Love me those side-effects, wouldn't want to program without 'em). I also find that whenever I skimp, it always comes back to bite me. And usually it was because I hadn't understood the problem-space well enough to write a proper test. That's one important part of TDD for me: I have to understand the requirements well enough to actually write a test for them. And the OP is also right in that Rails is a bad environment for TDD, as far as I can tell, because all the magic and auto-integration gets in the way and has to be laboriously stubbed/mocked etc. Maybe it's time the community got over Rails. (See also Uncle Bob's excellent architecture talk: [VIDEO] ).

comments.author: SevenNation
comments.story_title: Using a framework will harm the maintenance of your software
comments.why_zh: 关于把框架隔离在边界之外的可操作指导
comments.quote_zh: 有一个很棒的（虽然有点老）演讲叫“Architecture, the Lost Years”
comments.text_zh: > 很多人会争辩说，不用框架就意味着什么都要自己写。这是种虚假的二分法。我们完全可以正常使用库和框架。…… > 但我们应该在项目里给它们一个清晰、隔离良好的位置。…… 有一个很棒的（虽然有点老）演讲叫“Architecture, the Lost Years”，讲的正是这个问题，并给出了非常具体、可操作的指导：[VIDEO] 但怎么才能做到这种解耦呢？答案既显然又出人意料。划定一条边界。一边是框架，另一边是你的代码。穿过这条边界时，只允许哑数据结构通过。JSON 可以。struct 也可以。XML 也行。关键在于这些都是没有行为的数据块。这能给你带来很多好处。你可以让应用完全脱离网络、数据库和其他昂贵依赖来运行。于是测试就变得简单容易得多。当然，你也可以通过编写新的边界代码来替换掉框架。另一个重要教训与框架最初为什么会被加进项目有关。设计系统时，目标应该是尽可能久地推迟重大决策。因为那时候才能拿到最好的信息。有时候你可以一直推迟到这个问题变得无关紧要，这就是一场大胜。在被迫之前就伸手去拿框架，恰好会造成作者所谈论的那种局面。
comments.text: > Many people will argue that not using a framework means write everything yourself. This is a false dichotomy. We can use libraries and frameworks just fine. ... > But we should give them a clear, and well-isolated place in our project. ... There's an excellent, if older, presentation called "Architecture, the Lost Years" that addresses exactly this problem and gives very specific, actionable guidance on how to solve it: [VIDEO] But how to pull off this decoupling? The answer is both obvious and surprising. Define a boundary. On one side is the framework. On the other side is your code. Through the boundary, only dumb data structure can pass. JSON works. So do structs. So does XML. The point is that these are behaviorless blobs of data. This buys you a lot. You can run your application completely detached from the network, a database, and other expensive dependencies. So testing becomes much simpler and easier. And of course, you can replace the framework by writing new boundary code. The other big lesson has something to do with why frameworks get added to a project in the first place. When designing a system, the goal should be to defer major decisions for a long as possible. That's when the best information is available. Sometimes you can just defer until the point becomes moot, which is a major win. Reaching for a framework before being forced to do so sets up the kind of situation the author is talking about.

comments.quote_zh: 这里是 Uncle Bob 详细阐述他这个版本的想法：
comments.text_zh: 这里是 Uncle Bob 详细阐述他这个版本的想法：[VIDEO] 主要思路是把系统拆分成 entities、interactors 和 boundaries，它们大致对应 model、controllers 和 interfaces+DTOs（Data Transfer Objects），但不同之处在于，模型类不会通过接口暴露出来。相反，DTO 用来传达数据的变化。我们采用这种方法已经一年了，上面还架了 REST，到目前为止效果非常好。entities 能自然地映射到 REST 资源，DTO 则很适合作为请求和响应类。有了 CQRS（现在听起来很企业范儿），使用同样的 DTO 来处理数据存储就很容易（数据存储及其接口也对 entities 一无所知）。在数据库实现层面，我们操作 DTO，把它们存进数据库很轻松（即使不用 ORM 也行，尽管 ORM 确实能去掉很多样板代码）。只需要一个类——entity repository——把 DTO 转换成 entities，而且这只会发生在 create、update 和 delete 时。读取（由于 CQRS）直接走数据库，不实例化任何 entities——很妙。我们还使用 'unit of work' 模式来抽象 create、update 和 delete 操作中的事务概念，这简化了 interactor 代码，隐藏了数据存储的性质（在这方面也让它变得可替换）。但说回正题，我们的测试也很快，因为可以通过注入一个 in 来测试 interactors
comments.text: Here's Uncle Bob talking on his version of the idea extensively: [VIDEO] The main idea is to separate the system into entities, interactors and boundaries, which correspond roughly to model, controllers and interfaces+DTOs (Data Transfer Objects), but with the difference that model classes are not exposed through the interfaces. Rather, the DTOs are used to communicate the changes in the data. We have been using this approach for a year now, with REST on top, and it so far has worked beautifully. The entities map naturally to REST resources and DTOs makes nice request and response classes. Armed with CQRS (now I sound enterprise-y), the data storage is easy to work with using the same DTOs (the data storage and its interface do not know anything about the entities either). On the DB implementation level, we work on the DTOs, which are trivial to store to the database (even without ORM, although it does remove much of the boilerplate). Only one class - the entity repository - is needed to convert the DTOs to entities, and this only happens on create, update, and delete. Reads (due to CQRS) go directly to DB without instantiating any entities - neat. We also use 'unit of work' -pattern to abstract the notion of transaction on create, update, and delete operations, which simplifies the interactor code, hiding the nature of the data storage (making it a swappable in this respect too). comments.author: programminggeek
comments.why_zh: 关于面向值、无副作用的设计思路的演讲
comments.quote_zh: 有几场演讲围绕这种思路
comments.text_zh: 它可能会做那种极其低效的事……或者，你可以用一个指针列表，让某个指针指向另一个值，而不是去修改已有的值。我没有深入钻研过不可变数据结构如何能高效运作的细节，但它的魅力之一就在于，很多情况下你根本不需要修改数组。我的意思是，程序员之所以会做某些围绕修改的行为，只是因为他们能做。当你拿走修改数据的能力，你就会以不同的方式设计，而且没有副作用。突然间，你代码库中的很大一部分在测试上变得更简单、更快速、更便宜。你会得到更简单的解决方案，可能也更容易推理，因为那些复杂（有时优雅）的解法不再随手可得了。有几场演讲围绕这种思路：[链接] [视频] [链接] [链接] 边界是好的，值是好的，能协同工作的简单事物是好的。我们越能把好的部分组合成一个连贯的语言/框架/平台，我们的软件就会越好。
comments.text: It might do that wildly inefficient thing... Or, you might do something where you have a list of pointers, and you point at a different value instead of mutating an existing value. I haven't dug into the details of how immutable data structures can be made to work efficiently, but part of the charm is that in many cases you don't mutate the array at all. What I mean is, there are certain behaviors around mutation that programmers do because they can. When you take away the ability to mutate data, you design differently and without side effects. All of a sudden testing becomes easier, faster, cheaper for large parts of your codebase. You have simpler solutions that are potentially easier to reason about because the complex (and sometimes elegant) solutions aren't so readily available. A few talks that are around this style of thinking: [LINK] [VIDEO] [LINK] [LINK] Boundaries are good, values are good, simple things that work together are good. The more we can take the good parts and form them together into a cohesive language/framework/platform, the better our software will be.

comments.author: cellularmitosis
comments.story_title: My bag of tricks – loose notes, design patterns, rules-of-thumb
comments.why_zh: 帮助评论者理解了可测试代码的设计
comments.quote_zh: Uncle Bob 的这个“Architecture: the lost years”主题演讲对我很有帮助
comments.text_zh: Uncle Bob 的这个“Architecture: the lost years”主题演讲对我很有帮助：[VIDEO] 我也一直在纠结“不可测试”的代码这个概念。不可测试的代码通常似乎就是一大堆函数调用。可测试的代码似乎是一块块小功能孤岛，它们通过接口连接，只交换数据。实际上，这似乎就是要避免那些看起来像 'doThis()'、'doThat()' 的接口，而更像 'apply(data)'。少一些命令式的微观管理，多一些函数式核心/命令式外壳。补充：用网络来类比的话，可以想想远程过程调用 API 与单纯交换声明式数据（REST）之间的区别。
comments.text: This "Architecture: the lost years" keynote from uncle bob was helpful for me: [VIDEO] I've also struggled with this notion of "untestable" code. Untestable code seems to usually be a big pile of function calls. Testable code seems to be little islands of functionality which are connected by interfaces where only data is exchanged. Practically, this seems to be about shying away from interfaces which look like 'doThis()', 'doThat()', and more like 'apply(data)'. Less imperative micro-management and more functional-core/imperative-shell. Edit: a network analogy might be: think about the differences between a remote procedure call API vs. simply exchanging declarative data (REST).

comments.author: Barrera
comments.why_zh: 用哑数据结构把网络与逻辑解耦的出处
comments.quote_zh: 整个演讲都值得一看，以便把它放到上下文中理解。
comments.text_zh: > 尽管上面的设计从 OOP 的角度看完全成立，但这两个类其实都无法进行单元测试。因为 LocationProvider 依赖它自己的 HttpClient 实例，而 SolarCalculator 又依赖 LocationProvider，所以无法把这些类的方法里可能包含的业务逻辑隔离出来。这些类的设计很糟糕，而你觉得需要去用 mock（或接口）这件事本身就在告诉你这一点。作者接下来的做法是转向接口。换作我是不会这么做的。相反，我会用中间的哑数据结构把网络和计算解耦。网络这一侧产出该数据结构，计算这一侧消费它。网络这一侧还可以进一步拆解，把 API 调用结果转换成用于计算的哑数据结构。这个想法来自 Bob Martin 的一个老演讲 [1]。整个演讲都值得一看，以便把它放到上下文中理解。在这类推崇集成测试而非单元测试的文章里，这种事似乎从来不会被人讨论。想要更好的效果，就干脆丢掉类，只用函数。在“一切都是类”的模型下，设计跑偏的程度实在令人吃惊。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: > Although the design above is perfectly valid in terms of OOP, neither of these classes are actually unit-testable. Because LocationProvider depends on its own instance of HttpClient and SolarCalculator in turn depends on LocationProvider, it’s impossible to isolate the business logic that may be contained within methods of these classes. The design of those classes is bad, and the perceived need to reach for mocks (or interfaces) is telling you that. The next step the author takes is to go for interfaces. That's not what I'd do. Instead, I'd decouple network from calculation with intermediate dumb data structures. The network side produces the data structure and the calculation side consumes it. The network side can further be broken down with a transformation of the API call result into the dumb data structure used for calculations. This idea comes from an old Bob Martin presentation [1]. The whole thing is worth watching to put it into context. This is the kind of thing that never seems to get discussed in these pieces praising integration tests over unit tests. For even better results, ditch the classes altogether and just use functions. It's quite surprising how badly designs come off the rails with the "everything is a class" model. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.text: I think his first sentence is a strawman. What I'm tired of from the TDD crowd is that they insist that people are doing it wrong if they don't do to the extreme demand of others. A great example of this is Bob Martin saying that you are absolutely doing it wrong if you don't write your tests before your code and if you don't restrict your writing of app code to the pure case of making a failing test which you wrote first pass.
